name: type I restriction-modification target recognition
description: Recognition of the system's bipartite target sequence by the HsdS specificity subunit, which directs both the methyltransferase and the endonuclease. Which sequence is recognised is not claimed: HsdS specificity comes from variable target recognition domains that an orthology group does not resolve.

name: type I restriction-modification host protection
description: Adenine methylation of the host's own target sites by HsdM, without which the system would cleave the genome that encodes it.

name: type I restriction-modification DNA cleavage
description: ATP-dependent translocation and double-strand cleavage of unmethylated invading DNA by HsdR. It is required: a genome carrying only HsdM and HsdS has a methylation capability, which is real biology, but it defends against nothing and is not this claim.

name: type I-E Cascade surveillance complex
description: The five-subunit Cascade complex that binds crRNA and scans DNA for a matching protospacer. All five subunits are jointly required; the complex does not assemble without them.

name: type I-E interference nuclease
description: Recruitment of the Cas3 nuclease-helicase by target-bound Cascade, and processive degradation of the target. K07475, which identifies only the HD nuclease module of a split Cas3, is not accepted: it does not evidence the complete nuclease-helicase.

name: CRISPR spacer acquisition
description: Integration of new spacers by the Cas1-Cas2 integrase complex. It is accessory because a system can interfere using the spacers it already has, and cas1/cas2 are lost from many otherwise intact loci.
